# fabric_onelake_diagnostic_setting (Resource)

The OneLake Diagnostic Setting resource allows you to manage a Fabric [OneLake Diagnostic Setting](https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/fabric/core/onelake-settings/modify-diagnostics).

-> This resource supports Service Principal authentication.

**Important:** Destroying this resource disables OneLake diagnostics and clears the destination. Changing `workspace_id` also disables and clears diagnostics on the old workspace because the API does not expose a delete operation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "fabric_onelake_diagnostic_setting" "example" {
  workspace_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
  status       = "Enabled"

  destination = {
    lakehouse = {
      workspace_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
      item_id      = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `status` (String) The status of OneLake diagnostic logging. Possible values: `Enabled`, `Disabled`. Value must be one of : `Enabled`, `Disabled`.
- `workspace_id` (String) <i style="color:red;font-weight: bold">(ForceNew)</i> The ID of the source Workspace. The caller must have an Admin role on this Workspace.

### Optional

- `destination` (Attributes) The destination where OneLake diagnostic logs are stored. Required when diagnostics are enabled. When diagnostics are disabled, include the destination to retain it or omit it to clear it. The destination Lakehouse must be in the same capacity as the source Workspace, and the caller must have a Contributor or higher role on the destination Workspace. If the value of [`status`](#status) attribute is `Enabled` this attribute is **REQUIRED**. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destination))
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

<a id="nestedatt--destination"></a>

### Nested Schema for `destination`

Required:

- `lakehouse` (Attributes) The Lakehouse receiving OneLake diagnostic logs. The API currently supports references by ID only. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destination--lakehouse))

<a id="nestedatt--destination--lakehouse"></a>

### Nested Schema for `destination.lakehouse`

Required:

- `item_id` (String) The ID of the destination Lakehouse.
- `workspace_id` (String) The ID of the Workspace containing the destination Lakehouse.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>

### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# terraform import fabric_onelake_diagnostic_setting.example "<WorkspaceID>"
terraform import fabric_onelake_diagnostic_setting.example "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
```
